text:
pranav: Hey — I pushed a short PRD fragment for the smart routing + fallback sandbox acceptance checks. Need quick alignment on what we gate for launch. TL;DR: multi-tier, cross-region fallback, and model-compat checks (no customer-facing changes yet).
elsa: link? can you paste checklist here?
pranav: Sure — main items: 1) routing correctness (preferred tier honored), 2) failover latency SLOs, 3) model-compatibility policy (semantic-safe variants), 4) traffic split rollout + canary pass criteria, 5) regression tests for outputs for top 3 customers.
mike: For (2) what SLO do we expect? 95th perc < 200ms additional p99 < 400ms on failover?
pranav: My proposal: 95th additional latency <= 150ms, p99 <= 350ms. If failover triggers cross-region, add cap of 250ms extra at 95th (call out separately).
tara: We should be explicit about budget/cost gating. If fallback increases token-cost by >20% vs baseline, fail the rollout.
pranav: Agree. Add cost delta check as a hard gate.
ora: Edge cases: model-compat where tokenizer differs, or quantized weights lead to hallucination shifts. How do we detect that in sandbox?
elsa: We'll run automated evals on 4 buckets: semantic parity, safety regressions, latency-sensitive prompts, and reranking quality. Small prompt suite (200 examples) for canary.
ora: Ok but include one scenario where the fallback returns an incompatible shape (e.g., structured function-calling payload missing fields). Must fail closed.
pranav: Good call — acceptance criterion: any structural mismatch => rollback/skip fallback for that route.
mike: For rollout gating, propose these checks before 100%: a) functional tests pass, b) eval delta <= 1.5% for semantic, c) safety regressions = 0, d) cost delta <= 20%, e) failover latency gates met.
pranav: I'll add that to PRD. Also propose an automated replay test: synth spike for 20s at 2x normal QPS to ensure routing doesn't thrash.
tara: Add an operational guard: max fallback rate per route = 5% sustained, otherwise we trigger alert and auto-rollback.
ora: What about customer opt-outs? Some paying customers must not be routed to lower-tier variants. Need per-customer policy flag honored.
pranav: Yes — control plane must have per-customer affinity override. Default is allowed, but enterprise flag = no-fallback. Gate: verify that enterprise customers in test corpus remain on pinned model.
ora: Test data: include one real customer prompt set (anonymized) and two synthetic adversarial sets.
ora: Also include a YAML snippet for policy example.
pranav: paste: ```yaml
route: user-facing
preferred_tiers: [gold, standard]
fallback_order: [standard, burst]
no_fallback_customers: [cust-1234]
max_fallback_rate: 0.05
compatibility_checks: [tokenizer, response-schema, safety-check]
```
elsa: Nice. Add a check that fallback selection only chooses compatible model family (same API surface). If not, skip.
mike: Ops question: who runs the sandbox acceptance? eng-platform + SRE + QE?
pranav: Platform runs, QE triggers eval harness, SRE runs synthetic load and rollback automation. Need oncall to approve the final 2-hour canary window.
tara: Prioritization: customers asked for region-aware fallback and model-affinity. For v1 we do tiered fallback and enterprise opt-outs. Region affinity can be soft: prefer same-region but allow cross-region with stricter latency gate.
ora: So scope negotiation: drop cross-region blocking for v1 (allow but flag as higher-risk) and ship with strict SLOs.
ora: Add acceptance test for cross-region: when local pool is full, fallback to remote with latency logged and cost measured. If cross-region p95 extra > 200ms or cost delta >30% fail canary.
pranav: I also added rollout metrics: fallback_rate, avg_extra_latency, eval_semantic_delta, eval_safety_violations, cost_delta. These will appear in console per-route.
mike: We should have a temporary 'compatibility blacklist' to map model variants we know are incompatible. Maintain in config.
ora: Edge-case: model variant with function-calling signature change — treat as incompatible by default.
pranav: Acceptance criteria summary (short): - routing honors preference and enterprise opt-outs - automated evals: semantic delta <=1.5%, safety violations =0 - latency gates for local fallback (95th extra <=150ms) and cross-region (95th extra <=250ms) - cost delta <=20% - structural/shape mismatches cause skip/rollback - synthetic spike test pass - rollout metrics available and alerts wired.
elsa: LGTM. I'll add a line-item for audit logging (every fallback decision logged with reason + model ids).
pranav: Great. @deploy-bot can you create a sandbox run ticket after we finalize PRD?
deploy-bot: created ticket INF-4827 - smart-routing sandbox acceptance run — scheduled for 2026-03-22 10:00 UTC.
mike: Perfect. Timeline: finalize PRD today, sandbox run Tue, QE + SRE signoff Wed, canary Thu if all green.
pranav: Thanks everyone. I'll update the PRD and drop the link here when done. :thumbsup:
